examShortTricks: Trick 1: Distinguish the pair for the definition mark: humour amuses; satire CRITICISES through amusement — every unit question rewards naming the satire's TARGET.
Trick 2: Identify the devices: irony, exaggeration (hyperbole), parody, sarcasm — name the device AND the sentence that shows it.
Trick 3: When asked 'what is the writer satirising?', answer in one sentence naming the social vice (greed, hypocrisy, bureaucracy), not the plot.
practiceQuestions: Q. What is the difference between humour and satire? (2 marks) — humour entertains; satire exposes and criticises folly through humour.
Q. Name two satirical devices with an example from the text. (2 marks) — irony/hyperbole with the quoted line.
keyPoints: Humour entertains; satire criticises — identify the target of the joke in exam answers.
Quote the funny line, then explain what serious point it makes.
